title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0RB_1LA1LE_1LC0LA_1LF0RD_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0RB_1LA1LE_1LC0LA_1LF0RD_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

It is a counter in disguise. Each time the head reaches the left end, a solid block there has grown by six cells, and the next time takes four times as many steps. The head's excursions in between follow the carry pattern of a counter. A word on the right side of the tape changes a little at each overflow; when it is used up, the left block shrinks and a new epoch starts.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 2·1010 steps.

Where a halt would come from. The machine halts only in state F reading 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1LF), which is rare: 16 times in the first 108 steps, each time at the left end or in the run of 0s just left of the solid block, so F reads a 0.
What a proof needs. An exact description of one overflow (an induction over the counter's digits) and of the epoch change, showing that E reads a 0 only where the cell to its left is 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 134 cells have been visited and 51 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Overflows quadruple
claims.text: At the times state A is at the left end the tape starts A>0 1^n b … (b = 110), n growing by 6 per event; the gaps between events grow by a factor tending to 4: the events at steps 20,060,883, 78,781,139, 313,662,151, 1,253,186,235 and 5,011,282,607 have n = 60, 66, 72, 78, 84.

claims.title: Epochs
claims.text: The left block falls back from 1^39 to 1^18 at step 488,707 and from 1^84 to 1^75 at step 7,842,487,335, while the word on the right is rebuilt; between these the right word changes by a few cells per overflow.

claims.title: A counter
claims.text: Between overflows the head's rightward excursions from its home position have lengths 2, 4, 2, 6, 2, 4, 2, 8, …, and its leftward excursions grow in the same ruler pattern, the carries of a counter.

claims.title: E reads 0 only next to a 0
claims.text: F, the state with the halting transition, is entered only from E reading 0. In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps that happens 16 times: 12 at the left end of the tape and 4 in the run of 0s left of the solid block, always with a 0 to the left, so F reads 0.

claims.title: A run-length frame map, every case proved
claims.text: At every head turn write the tape as two lists of runs (blocks of equal cells), left and right of the head: a frame with list parameters. A table of 310 cases, each a pattern on the first few runs of both sides (lengths exact or at least 4, the rest of each side any list), sends each frame to the frame of the next head turn; every case is proved for all values of its parameters and all lists by one symbolic run (RLCase.sound), so the frame map next = rlNext cases is sound (rlNext_sound). Between two head turns this machine crosses only a few run boundaries, which is why a finite table covers a tape whose number of runs grows without bound.
claims.where: cases, lean/Cases.lean; the runs in lean/Pieces.lean; generated by py/frames.py lean with tools/py/bbtools/listframe.py; library tools/lean/TM/ListFrame.lean

claims.title: The frame map from blank tape
claims.text: The run from blank tape reaches the first frame (init_f0, kernel), and the frame map is defined for its first 100,000 frames (native_decide). If it is defined forever along this orbit, the machine never halts (no_halt_of_total).

claims.title: The case table covers the run
claims.text: Every frame at a head turn in the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps (1,500,084 head turns) is matched by a case, and the case's next frame is the machine's (no mismatch, no unmatched frame); 299 cases at 10<sup>6</sup> steps, 310 at 3·10<sup>6</sup>, so a longer run may need more.

claims.title: No finite frame map with scalar parameters
claims.text: The frame-map method (stop at head turns, match the tape against finitely many templates with block-length parameters, fit affine cases) needs the tapes at head turns to fall into a bounded number of shapes. Here they do not: tokenizing the tape at every 7th head turn into maximal powers of words of length at most 4, the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps give 617,359 distinct shapes (exponents of 3 and more merged), 553,191 of them new in the last decade, and up to 34 tokens per tape; the number grows tenfold per decade of steps. For comparison the same count saturates at 32 shapes of at most 5 tokens for 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC and at 89 for 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_0RE1LD_0LB1LD_---1RC_1RA0RD, where frame maps were proved. The cause is the counter itself: its digits form an arbitrary word, and the word of higher digits on the right grows too, so a frame needs a list parameter; the run-length frames above are such frames.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The run looks like a counter that runs forever, but the epoch change has not been described exactly.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a counter whose overflows come four times further apart each time. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Each overflow at the left end takes about four times as long as the last.
The block at the left end grows by six cells per overflow.

sections.heading: A counter that slows down by four
html: Watch the left end of the tape. Every so often the head arrives there in state A, and each time the solid block of 1s at the left end has grown by six cells: A>0 1^60 … at step 20,060,883, A>0 1^66 … at 78,781,139, then 1^72 at 313,662,151, 1^78 at 1,253,186,235 and 1^84 at 5,011,282,607. The gaps grow by a factor of 4, so the tape grows like the logarithm of the time: about 130 cells after 109 steps.

In between, the head stays near a home position and makes excursions of lengths 2, 4, 2, 6, 2, 4, 2, 8, … cells: the carries of a counter. Each overflow also changes the right part of the tape, a word made of 10, 110 and short blocks of 1s, by a few cells.

When that word has been worked through, the run starts a new epoch: at step 488,707 the left block drops from 1^39 to 1^18, and at step 7,842,487,335 from 1^84 to 1^75, with a new, longer word on the right.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The only halting transition is F reading a 1, and F is entered only when E reads a 0 and steps left. E reads a 0 only 16 times in 108 steps, at the left end or in the 0s just left of the solid block, and F then reads a 0. A halt would need E to meet a 0 with a 1 to its left; the counter's structure never offers that, but this is not proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 134 cells (125 left of the start, 8 right), with a density of 1s of 0.381.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A counter whose overflows at the left end come four times further apart each time (the left block grows by 6 cells per overflow); a slowly changing word on the right ends each epoch.
